_about: The sights. clickMoa is what one click of elevation moves the strike, windageClickMoa one click of windage, in minutes of angle; clicks is the travel each way from the middle. zoom is the magnification range; fovFtAt100 the field of view in feet at 100 yards at the lowest and highest zoom. frontPostMoa is the front post's width over the sight radius (how wide it looks against the target); apertureMoa the rear ring's lit circle and notchMoa the rear notch's width as the eye sees them; dotMoa a red dot's size. leaf is a sliding rear leaf: its marked settings, the service load it was cut for, and each setting's angle above the 100 m setting, derived with the engine (leaf545: the same leaf on the 5.45x39 rifle, cut for its own load). notchDepthMoa is the rear notch's depth as the eye sees it; stemWidthMoa a bead's stem; a drop reticle's chevronHalfWidthMoa and markHalfWidthMoa are its drawn widths. aimWanderFactor scales the drawn wander of the aim through this sight (1 where absent). frontBead marks a front sight that is a round bead on a stem rather than a flat post. range-day-twelve: sightRadiusIn is the distance between the front and rear sight, the radius the front post's width is seen over; frontPostIn and apertures (each peep's diameterIn) are the parts' own sizes; frontEars draws the front sight's guards (their inner gap, each one's width, and how far their tops stand above the post); frontStripeMoa and frontStripeTopMoa a glowing stripe on a front post; adjustWords says in plain words where each adjustment is; kind "seeall" is the SeeAll Open Sight, its reticle a triangle whose tip is the aim point, standing across a line that tops a glowing field; a reticle's focalPlane and trueAtPower say where a second-focal-plane reticle's marks are true (at another power p they stand trueAtPower / p times as far apart in angle). tookThePlaceOf names the sight a new one replaced on its rifles without carrying its records (they click differently or sit at another height): a record from before any sight could be chosen, made with the old sight, is never read as the new one's. rearBody is a rear peep's leaf, where it stands far from the eye (its width and how far its top stands above the peep): only the leaf is dark around the peep; a sight without it has its ring close to the eye, dark to the edges of the view. range-day-twelve-b: a rear sight with two peeps (apertures, each with its diameterIn and the apertureMoa it covers seen from the eye) flips between them on the firing line; both stand in the same plane, so the flip moves no shot. frontHood is a round hood around the front post (its inside diameter and its wall, as the eye sees them), centred on the post's tip.

Chosen because Dan named "Troy Industries Folding Battle Sight Rear" and "Troy folding rear and front"; of Troy's two folding fronts (HK-style round hood, M4-style ears) Dan remembers the round one (21 Nov 2026: "I think it was round"); the tritium and diamond-aperture versions were not named. range-day-twelve-b: the M4-style front drawn before carried the same A2 post, clicks and height, so no record changes.

Troy gives no figure; retailers' "0.5 MOA per click" does not fit an A2 post's mechanics and is not used. Magpul, whose MBUS front takes the same A2 post, gives 1.886 in at 100 m per click on a carbine (https://magpul.com/mbus-sight-front.html, search text): 1.886 / 3937 radians over a 14.5 in radius is 0.00695 in of post travel per click; over this rifle's 18 in radius that is 1.33 MOA

ak762-kns-peep.name: AK ball front post (KNS 0.034 in) and KNS adjustable rear peep
ak762-kns-peep.model: Front: KNS Precision ball post AKBALL.034. Rear: KNS Precision AK Adjustable Rear Peep Sight, part AK EL-WIN ("for AKM-Style Rear Sight", https://www.midwestgunworks.com/page/mgwi/prod/akel-win, search text), which takes the rear leaf's place: a peep hole in a leaf, a notched wheel and index marks, as the photographs show.
